When_a_HTTP_request_is_received.description: Call this before executing any step of an autonomous or multi-step agent loop (before each reasoning step, tool call, or retry). It enforces a hard budget on how many steps a single agent session may take, preventing runaway loops. Pass a session_id that uniquely identifies the current agent conversation or run; this tool increments that session's step counter and reports whether the session is still within budget. If the response has allowed: false, you MUST stop the loop immediately and return the 'reason' field to the user or calling agent instead of taking further action — do not call this tool merely to check status without intending to honor a stop response. Call loop-budget-reset once at the start of a new session before the first call to this tool, or it will inherit a stale counter from a previous run.

session_id.description: A unique identifier for the current agent session or conversation. Reuse the exact same value across every step of the same loop so the budget is tracked correctly. Use a new, different value for a new conversation.

max_steps.description: The maximum number of steps allowed for this session before this tool reports allowed: false. Optional — if omitted, defaults to 25. Only meaningful on the first call for a session (when no row exists yet); later calls should omit it and rely on the value set at loop-budget-reset time.

Get_Entity.description: UNVERIFIED SHAPE — this is a best-effort reconstruction of the Azure Tables built-in connector's 'Get Entity' action, not confirmed against a live deployment. If this action shows an error in the designer after pasting (e.g. a red exclamation mark, or 'invalid template' on save), delete just this action and re-add 'Azure Tables -> Get Entity' via the designer's connector picker instead, filling in: Table name = LoopBudgets, Partition key = session, Row key = the expression triggerBody()?['session_id']. Everything else in this file does not depend on the internals of this action, only on its outputs, so replacing just this one action is safe.

Fallback if this errors: re-add 'Azure Tables -> Insert or Update Entity' via the designer, Table name = LoopBudgets, Partition key = session, Row key = triggerBody()?['session_id'], then set the entity properties StepCount/MaxSteps/LastUpdated to the expressions shown in this action's 'entity' parameter below.

body.reason: Step budget exceeded for this session. Halt the loop and report this to the user instead of continuing.
